record_notes.DCP-LETT-1823: January22, supplied1856; six blocks, seven notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing Henslow note and corrects own forgetting earlier carnation-seed news. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1903: June16, supplied1856; all five blocks, full notes and bibliography read. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1936: August2,1856 incomplete damaged letter; both retained blocks, seven notes, annotations and bibliography read. Aegilops wheat-like plant netted but feared infertile, hybrid possibility explicitly retained; not established transformation into wheat. record_notes.DCP-LETT-2006: AfterDecember6,1856 fragment; all three blocks, five notes and bibliography read. record_notes.DCP-LETT-2329: September25, supplied1857; all four blocks, four notes and bibliography read. NumericID2329 does not override documented1857date. record_notes.DCP-LETT-2154: October18, supplied1857; six blocks, five notes and bibliography read. Thanks missing intervening Henslow note, proposed photograph delivery not received. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1778: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 10, supplied 1855 heading. Thanks for newly received experimental seeds and encloses ten-shilling postal order. Reports that only one of thirty or forty tested plants remained afloat after a month, while capsicum/celery seeds germinated after 137 days of salt immersion; distinguish flotation from germination and revised expectation from a disproof of all sea transport. Has already sent Vilmorin a note. Lychnis whiteness and counting both parsnip seeds are explicit assumptions pending correction. Requests forwarding hollyhock queries to a grower. The surviving related draft 1779 is dated November 12, so dispatch/assembly cannot safely be set to November 10 solely from heading. Actual dispatched fair copy is unlocated.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1779: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 12, 1855 is written at the end of the draft questions. Recto draft covering letter to Henslow and verso questions are a single draft enclosure associated with 1778, not an incoming Henslow or Chater letter. Questions ask whether kinds come true, whether separation from bees matters, and whether controlled crosses give intermediate colours. These are enquiries and reports of prior authors, not grower answers. Circled inserted a before first question may refer to another intended question; do not invent it or assert final dispatched copy exactly matches draft. Header Nov.— is less complete than closing dateline.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1797: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 18 with supplied month/year. Three blocks acknowledge safely received seeds and refer to Henslow forthcoming busy week. London Friday visit is prospective; footnote records attendance Thursday December 20, which is a distinct event and must not be substituted for the stated plan. No source body for Henslow seed dispatch or schedule survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1801: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 26, supplied 1855. Forwards unidentified club book borrowed from Innes and seeks advice about solvency, actuary assessment, withholding future pensions and buying out distant members. Explicitly says the club has not yet granted a pension. Proposed rule and actuarial consultation are not completed actions; no Henslow reply is present. Earlier benefit-club correspondence is background, not this missing answer.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
